message.reasoning:
We need to judge each finding against sealed bugs E1–E7, plus confirmed properties P1–P6 and open item O1 (not detailed here, but referenced). We only know sealed bugs E1-E7. P1-P6 and O1 content not given; we can't name properties unless obvious. The instructions say flag if contradicting a confirmed property — we don't know them, so mostly null.

Map findings:

F01: out-of-order completion, wrap of currentLogBlock, TranCommitted/EarlierPassno arithmetic — forced commit returns before END on disk; silent-loss of acknowledged commit. Sealed: E1 is io_window count/distance confusion, fail-stop, own. F01's mechanism is different (pass wrap in commit test), effect silent-loss vs fail-stop. Contract: none violated (out-of-order permitted). E2 is durability of completed write — not this. So no match? Mechanism differs, effect differs. Contract "none violated" same as E1/E6/E7 but mechanism and effect differ. Ruling: no match. Could argue partial with E1 (same contract: out-of-order permitted, own defect) — partial requires contract and one of other two, or right mechanism under different contract. Contract is "none violated" for both F01 and E1; mechanism differs; effect differs. So no match. Hmm, but "same violated contract" — both have no contract violated, both own defects in out-of-order handling. Partial? Effect: E1 fail-stop, F01 silent-loss. Mechanism: E1 io_window count/distance; F01 EarlierPassno wrap. Different. I'd say no match.

F02: C021 checksum unknown version fail-open, torn page replayed, silent wrong value. Sealed: none of E1-E7 covers checksum config. E4? E4 is lost metadata write masked by redo — different. No match.

F03: out-of-order first pages, clean log skip recovery, pass collision between incarnations, stale pages splice, MarkCommitted by tran id. This resembles E6: clean-mount path starts pass R+1 at slot 0 without persisting; after crash, out-of-order landing and second clean mount, two runs' pages share pass number — silent-splice. F03: page 0 still holds restart record → treated clean, passno = IncPassno(restart pass), same pass as crashed incarnation; stale page joins; silent-splice (uncommitted update redone). Same contract (none violated, own), same mechanism (pass collision after clean mount without recovery), same effect class (silent-splice / silent-atomicity). Match E6. Also E7? E7 is pass-range masking in head search — different. Match E6.

F04: C024 metadataOK premature kill, committed update lost. Sealed: none. E4 is disk lost write; F04 is caller contract violation (env). No match.

F05: C088 — but mechanism is decayed head page, in-transit window converts damage to "not written", committed END dropped. Wait, F05 says violated C088 (log container overwrite) but mechanism is bit decay/overwrite of head page. Actually C088 is about log resize/overwrite by file data. F05's mechanism: completed head page overwritten (no magic, bad checksum), head-window rule truncates. Effect silent-loss of acknowledged commit. Sealed: E1? E1 is io_window count/distance, fail-stop. Not same. E2 durability? No, page was completed then overwritten — that's like C071 (preserve completed writes). Hmm F05 cites C088 but mechanism matches C071-ish. Against sealed: no match. Effect silent-loss; no sealed bug with that mechanism. No match.

F06: C018 stale read of log head, older well-formed page accepted, committed update undone. Sealed: none matches (E7 head misidentification? E7: masked comparison reads old page as newer — head misidentified. F06: stale read returns older page, accepted as head. Mechanism: E7 is pass-counter arithmetic in head search; F06 is device returning stale data. Different contract (env vs own). Effect: F06 silent-loss; E7 fail-stop/uncertain. Partial? "right mechanism under a different contract" — mechanism not same. Contract+one other? Contract differs. No match.

F07: hole at first crash, checkpoint written at hole, second recovery takes stale page as head, partial redo, reverses abort decision. Sealed: E1? E1 is io_window count/distance causing spurious RCVR_IOERR — fail-stop. F07: checkpoint block written into hole makes binary search pass over hole — different mechanism, silent effect. E6? pass collision? Not really. No match... Could be partial to E1 (both involve holes/in-transit window and head search, own defect)? E1's mechanism: io_window used as distance vs count. F07 doesn't involve io_window. No match.

F08: C041 AIX ESOFT cleared, force reported success, WAL broken, uncommitted value on disk. Sealed: E2/E3? E3: stolen uncommitted metadata page reaches media while undo record only in cache — silent-atomicity, env, disk durability. F08: log force falsely successful, home write proceeds, log record not durable — uncommitted value survives, empty log. Effect silent-atomicity (uncommitted change survives). Contract: driver/async layer env. E3's contract is disk durability; F08's is async layer clearing error. Mechanism differs (E3: steal before undo durable; F08: error cleared). Effect class same (silent-atomicity). Partial: contract and one of other two? Contract different. "right mechanism under different contract"? No. Hmm. Effect same only → no match per rules (need contract + one of mechanism/effect, or mechanism + different contract). Neither holds. No match. Though arguably E2 (acknowledged commit lost)? F08's effect is uncommitted data visible, not committed lost. No match.

F09: C058 forged restart marker, clean log skip recovery, uncommitted value survives. Sealed: none about restart authenticity. E6 involves clean-mount pass but different. No match.

F10: C071 decayed head page, in-transit scan truncates, commits lost. Same as F05 essentially. Sealed: no match. E1? E1's io_window confusion — F10's mechanism is the head-window rule treating bad checksum as in-flight. Different. No match.

Flag confirmed properties: we don't know P1-P6 contents; can't flag. Open item O1 unknown; none seem to address it.

F03 match E6 — check effect: E6 silent-splice; F03 effect "recovery reports success but metadata holds update of transaction that never ended" — silent-splice/atomicity. Match.

Write JSON.
